title: Live pokes from the vault: `GET /v1/sync/live` on the Hibernation API
heading: Task 10: Live pokes from the vault: `GET /v1/sync/live` on the Hibernation API
text:
**Starts after:** 1A-T3, 1A-T5, 1A-T8, 1B-T3

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/edge/src/vault/live.ts`
- Modify: `apps/edge/src/vault/user-vault.ts` (`fetch`, the WebSocket handlers, the auto-response, and the poke and close around `call()` and `alarm()`), `src/v1/routes.ts` (`VaultRoute.live`, the route, `VAULT_ADDED_ROUTES`), `src/v1/handler.ts` (the live branch), `src/cloudflare-workers.d.ts`, `test/workers/support/v1-client.ts` (`openLive`), `test/vault-route-coverage.test.ts` (after 1B-T13, `test/route-coverage.test.ts`)
- Test: `apps/edge/test/workers/live.test.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `UserVault`, `VaultContext`, `ensureAccount`, `assertSession`, `RateBuckets`, `toProblemReply`, `handleVaultV1`, `VAULT_V1_ROUTES` and `VaultRoute` (`src/v1/routes.ts`), `VaultClaims` (1A-T2, with 1B-T3's `authTime`); commits under `sync_state.revision` (1A-T3); `UserVault#alarm` and the retention change groups (1A-T8); `UserVault#erased` (1B-T2) and `call()`'s erased refusal (1B-T3); `newUser`, `startV1`, `member`, `vaultOf` and `TestUser = { sub, sid }` (1A's test support), `createLunch` (1A-T5).
- Produces:
  ```ts
  // src/vault/live.ts
  export type LiveAttachment = { sessionId: string; issuedAt: number; openedAt: number }
  export const LIVE_CLOSE = { sessionEnded: 4401, replaced: 4409, unexpected: 1008 } as const
  export const MAX_LIVE_SOCKETS = 20
  export function currentRevision(sql: SqlStorage): string                   // CAST(revision AS TEXT); '0' without a row
  export function pokeMessage(revision: string): string                      // '{"revision":"<r>"}'
  export function pokeOthers(state: DurableObjectStateLike, revision: string, exceptSession: string | null): number
  export function closeEndedSessions(state: DurableObjectStateLike, sql: SqlStorage, erased: boolean): number
  export function parseLiveClaims(header: string | null): VaultClaims | null  // every VaultClaims field checked
  export function acceptLive(state: DurableObjectStateLike, claims: VaultClaims, nowMs: number): Response
  // UserVault
  fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response>      // only GET https://vault.internal/live with upgrade: websocket and x-vault-claims
  webSocketMessage(ws: WebSocket, message: string | ArrayBuffer): void
  webSocketClose(ws: WebSocket, code: number, reason: string, wasClean: boolean): void
  webSocketError(ws: WebSocket, error: unknown): void
  private afterCall(before: string, sessionId: string | null): void   // poke when the revision grew, then close ended sessions; never throws
  // src/v1/routes.ts (where VaultRoute lives)
  VaultRoute gains live?: true                    // answered by UserVault#fetch as a WebSocket: no vault call, no Worker handler
  export const VAULT_ADDED_ROUTES: readonly string[]   // routes the PostgreSQL edge never had: ['GET /v1/sync/live']; 1D-T11 adds 'GET /v1/me/analytics'
  // test/workers/support/v1-client.ts
  export type LiveTestSocket = { messages: string[]; next(timeoutMs?: number): Promise<string>; closed: Promise<{ code: number }>; send(data: string): void; close(): void }
  export function openLive(client: V1Client, user: TestUser, opts?: { client?: string }): Promise<{ status: number; body?: unknown; socket?: LiveTestSocket }>
  ```
- The Hibernation API calls are Cloudflare's (developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/state and /best-practices/websockets): `ctx.acceptWebSocket(ws, tags)` (at most 10 tags of 256 characters), `ctx.getWebSockets(tag?)`, `ctx.getTags(ws)`, `ctx.setWebSocketAutoResponse(new WebSocketRequestResponsePair('ping', 'pong'))` (answered without waking the object), `ws.serializeAttachment(value)` and `ws.deserializeAttachment()` (at most 16,384 bytes, kept through hibernation), and `new Response(null, { status: 101, webSocket: client })` from the object's `fetch`. With a compatibility date from 2026-04-07 on, the runtime answers a Close frame itself, so `webSocketClose` need not call `close`.
- Rules:
  - The route `{ method: 'GET', path: '/v1/sync/live', access: 'bound_session', live: true }`, with no gate, is in `VAULT_V1_ROUTES` and in `VAULT_ADDED_ROUTES`.
  - **The branch in `handleVaultV1` sits immediately before the vault call,** after every check that comes before one: route, body, gates, client version, token, and 1C-T10a's `accountGate` (whichever of 1D-T10 and 1C-T10a lands second keeps this order; 1B-T3's Worker-route dispatch stays where 1B put it). An erased or deleting account therefore never reaches `UserVault#fetch`, whose `ensureAccount` would re-create `account_state` (C17). The `!route.vault` guard lets a `live` route through. A `live` route requires `upgrade: websocket` (compared case-insensitively), else 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` (never 426, which the app reads as "update the app"). It then returns `stub.fetch(new Request('https://vault.internal/live', { headers: { upgrade: 'websocket', 'x-vault-claims': JSON.stringify(claims) } }))` unchanged. The token never reaches the vault, and only the Worker can build this request: the object has no public route.
  - **`UserVault#fetch`** answers 404 to anything else. An erased vault answers 403 `ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE` before it touches a table, as 1B-T3's `call()` does. `parseLiveClaims` requires `accountId` and `sessionId` to be UUIDs, `issuedAt` an integer, `clientId` a non-empty string and `authTime` an integer when present; otherwise 400. Then, inside one `transactionSync` as `call()` runs them: the `VaultContext` (policies `null`), `ensureAccount`, the `principal` charge, `assertSession` and the `read` charge, on the same `RateBuckets`. A refusal answers `toProblemReply`'s problem as JSON with its status and never upgrades. Then `acceptLive`.
  - **`acceptLive`** closes this session's earlier sockets with 4409 (`getWebSockets(sessionId)`), accepts the new one with tags `[sessionId]` and its attachment, then, while more than `MAX_LIVE_SOCKETS` sockets are open (`readyState === WebSocket.OPEN`; a closing socket does not count), closes the oldest by `openedAt` with 4409.
  - The constructor sets the `ping`/`pong` auto-response. `webSocketMessage` closes with 1008 whatever reaches it (a `ping` never does). `webSocketClose` and `webSocketError` do nothing.
  - **Around `call()`** (and 1D-T11's `callWithAnalytics`), in this order: refuse an erased vault (1B-T3); read `before = currentRevision(sql)` outside the transaction; run the transaction and its `catch` unchanged; then, whatever the outcome, `afterCall(before, claims.sessionId)`: read `after`, and when `BigInt(after) > BigInt(before)` (only a committed transaction moves it) call `pokeOthers(ctx, after, claims.sessionId)`; then `closeEndedSessions(ctx, sql, false)`. `afterCall` never throws: a failure is logged as `live_after_call_failed` with `failureName`, and the reply goes back unchanged. So a refused call (a raised `not_before`, a revoked session, an account being deleted) still closes the sockets it ended.
  - `alarm()` does the same around its work, with `exceptSession` `null`, so a retention purge pokes every phone.
  - **`closeEndedSessions(state, sql, erased)`:** with `erased`, every socket closes with 4401 and no table is read. Otherwise it reads `account_state`'s `status` and `not_before` (a missing row counts as not active). When the account is not `active`, every socket closes with 4401. Otherwise a socket closes with 4401 when its attachment's `issuedAt` is before `not_before` or its session is in `revoked_sessions`. The revoked check is one query that binds the open sockets' session ids as one JSON parameter: `SELECT session_id FROM revoked_sessions WHERE session_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))` with `JSON.stringify(ids)` (R57).
  - A send or close that throws (a socket already closing) is skipped, and the loop goes on.
  - A socket may outlive its token: it carries no data, and it closes only when its session ends, its session opens another, or the phone closes it (L1).
  - `cloudflare-workers.d.ts` gains only: on `DurableObjectStateLike`, `acceptWebSocket`, `getWebSockets`, `getTags` and `setWebSocketAutoResponse`; the globals `WebSocketPair` and `WebSocketRequestResponsePair`; on `WebSocket`, `accept`, `readyState`, `serializeAttachment` and `deserializeAttachment`; `webSocket` on `ResponseInit` and `Response`.
  - **The route coverage test** accepts the added routes. Each `VAULT_ADDED_ROUTES` key is served, absent from the PostgreSQL route table, and never shadowed by a legacy route (`matchRoute` over the legacy table finds none of them). `listed.filter((key) => !legacy.has(key))` equals the added keys instead of `[]`. The access, gates and status loop, and the list of ported routes, skip them. A `live` route has neither `vault` nor `worker`, so 1B-T3's "exactly one of" rule gains this exception beside `GET /v1/policies`. After 1B-T13 these checks move into `test/route-coverage.test.ts`, beside `VAULT_EDGE_ONLY_ROUTES`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests** in `test/workers/live.test.ts` with `openLive`. It signs the token as `client.as(user)` does, sends `upgrade: websocket` and `x-gogospend-client`, calls `accept()` on the returned socket and records its messages (Cloudflare's pattern, developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/examples/testing-with-durable-objects). A second session of the same person is `{ ...user, sid: crypto.randomUUID() }`, as 1A's logout test makes one.
  - `the other phone hears the new revision, and the saving phone hears nothing`: sessions A and B, both open; A creates a wallet; B's next message is exactly `{"revision":"<the ack's committed_revision>"}`; A has received nothing 200 ms later.
  - `a poke reaches a phone whose socket hibernated`: B open, `evictDurableObject(vaultOf(user), { webSockets: 'hibernate' })` (in 1.4.7's types), then A writes and B gets the poke.
  - `sockets never carry record data`: across a create, an update and a delete, every message B receives matches `/^\{"revision":"(0|[1-9][0-9]*)"\}$/`.
  - `ping is answered, even after the vault sleeps`: `ping` gives `pong` before and after the eviction.
  - `signing out closes that phone's socket with 4401 and leaves the other open`: B posts `/v1/me/logout`; B's socket closes with 4401; A still gets `pong`.
  - `a refused call still closes the sockets it ended`: raise `account_state.not_before` through `runInDurableObject`; A's next call is refused with 401 `SESSION_REQUIRED`, and A and B both close with 4401. A second case sets `status = 'deleting'`: the call is 403 and both close.
  - `an ended session cannot open a socket`: after logout, `openLive` answers 401 `SESSION_REQUIRED` and no socket.
  - `an erased vault cannot open a socket, and nothing is re-created`: after `vaultOf(user).erase()` (1B-T2), `openLive` answers 403 `ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE` with no socket.
  - `without a token it is 401, an outdated client 426, and a plain GET 400`
  - `a session's second socket replaces its first`: the first closes with 4409.
  - `only open sockets count toward 20`: twenty sessions open; one phone closes its socket; two more sessions open: exactly one socket closes with 4409, the oldest still-open one.
  - `a retention purge pokes every phone`: with the vault clock moved past 30 days, `runDurableObjectAlarm` gives A and B the purge's revision.
  - `a message other than ping closes the socket with 1008`
  - In the coverage test: `an added route is served, is not in the legacy table, and shadows no legacy route`, and `a live route has neither a vault call nor a Worker handler`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run them and see them fail** (the route is 404). Run: `npm run test:edge:workers -- test/workers/live.test.ts` and `npm run test:edge -- test/vault-route-coverage.test.ts`. Record the counts.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `live.ts`, the vault methods, the order around `call()` and `alarm()`, the Worker branch and the coverage rules, as above. Until 1B-T13 lands, `/v1/*` reaches `handleVaultV1` through `src/roles/vault.ts`; 1D-T12 adds the HTTP Worker's entry.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run them and see them pass.** Then the whole Workers suite: 1A's and 1B's tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] **Step 5: Mutation check.** Poke the sender too: the first test fails. Close ended sessions inside the `try`, so only a successful call closes them: the refused-call test fails. Put the snapshot in the poke: the no-record-data test fails. Accept before `assertSession`: the ended-session test fails. Check `erased` after `ensureAccount`: the erased test fails (500, the tables are gone). Count closing sockets toward the limit: the limit test fails.
- [ ] **Step 6: Gate, receipt, commit.** Commit: `Poke a person's other phones from their UserVault over hibernating WebSockets after each commit, and close ended sessions after every call`.

  // UserVault
  callWithAnalytics(call: VaultCall): { reply: VaultReply; analytics: VaultAnalytics }   // call(x) returns callWithAnalytics(x).reply
  // src/vault/analytics.ts

  export function committedEvents(c: VaultContext, route: VaultRouteId, before: string, after: string): ServerEvent[]
  export function weeksSinceSignup(c: VaultContext): number                     // whole weeks since account_state.created_at, at most 1040
  // src/v1/handler.ts

  // test/workers/support/v1-client.ts

- Rules:
  - **The route** `{ method: 'GET', path: '/v1/me/analytics', access: 'bound_session', vault: 'me.analytics' }` joins `VAULT_ADDED_ROUTES`. The vault handler answers `200 { weeks_since_signup, consent }`. For this route only, the Worker adds `analytics_id`: `await analyticsIdFor(claims.accountId, env.ANALYTICS_ID_KEY)` when the key is set, else `null` (the app then stays anonymous, and 1D-T3's deletion has nothing to delete).   - **`callWithAnalytics`** runs `call()`'s steps in 1D-T10's order and returns, beside the reply, what it read after the transaction (a refusal commits nothing, so those reads see the state before): `consent` (`'unasked'` whenever the account could not be read), `events` from `committedEvents(c, call.route, before, after)`, and `failure`, the `failureName` that `toProblemReply` logs for a 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` reply, else `null`. 1A's tests that call `call()` see no change.
  - **`committedEvents`** answers nothing unless the route is `transactions.create` (imports and other writers never count, decided, Q16). For that route it reads `SELECT snapshot FROM entity_changes WHERE entity = 'transaction' AND version = 1 AND state = 'active' AND revision > CAST(?1 AS INTEGER) AND revision <= CAST(?2 AS INTEGER)`: a revision range with two parameters, never an id list (R57). Each row gives one `record_saved` `{ kind, category_key }`, with `kind` from the snapshot's `type` and `category_key` from `categoryById(c, id)?.builtin_key ?? 'custom'` (one id per call); a transfer sends `{ kind: 'transfer' }` with no category. A resent command commits nothing, so it sends nothing.

Server events carry `origin: 'server'`, so dashboards tell them from the app's events of the same name.
    - `captureFailure(failure ?? 'Error', route.vault)` runs only for a 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` reply, whatever the consent (an anonymous class-name count). In the outer `catch`, an error that is not a `ProblemException` runs `captureFailure(failureName(error), 'worker')`. A deliberate refusal (a paused gate's 503, 401, 403, 426, 429) is never counted.

Each test that needs them passes them per test: `startV1(config, { env: { POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN: 'phc_test', ANALYTICS_ID_KEY: 'test-analytics-key' }, analytics: (env) => createServerAnalytics(env, (p) => pending.push(p), () => fakePort) })`, where `fakePort` records each `captureImmediate` message. Without a token the default dep builds no client. This also keeps `ANALYTICS_ID_KEY` unset for 1C's deletion tests, whose step 6 then answers `nothing_to_delete` without a request (1D-T13).

  export function serveV1(request: Request, env: V1Env, ctx?: { waitUntil(promise: Promise<unknown>): void }): Promise<Response>

title: Account deletion deletes the PostHog person (1C's step 6), retried daily after the sweep
heading: Task 13: Account deletion deletes the PostHog person (1C's step 6), retried daily after the sweep
text:
**Starts after:** 1D-T3, 1C-T11

**Files:**
- Modify: `apps/edge/src/analytics/server-analytics.ts` (exports `deletePostHogPersonById`, the request part of 1D-T3's `deletePostHogPerson`, which then calls it; 1D-T3's tests stay unchanged and green), `apps/edge/src/deletion/hooks.ts` (1C's no-op hook replaced), `apps/edge/src/deletion/workflow.ts` (`DeletionEnv` gains the four secrets; step 6 becomes `analytics-id` and `delete-analytics-person`; the retry loop after `final-sweep`)
- Test: `apps/edge/test/server-analytics.test.ts` (one case), `apps/edge/test/workers/deletion.test.ts` (1C's file: new cases, and any case that lists `DELETION_STEPS` updated in the same commit)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `analyticsIdFor`, `deletePostHogPerson`, `AnalyticsDeletionFailed`, `PersonDeletion`, `createServerAnalytics`, `PostHogPort`, `ServerAnalyticsEnv` (1D-T3); `DeletionWorkflow`, `DeletionEnv`, `DELETION_STEPS`, `STEP_CONFIG`, the reader 1C-T11's steps use to get the user id from `deletion_requests` by request id, and the deletion test helpers (1C-T11).
- Produces:
  ```ts
  // src/analytics/server-analytics.ts (1D-T3's module)
  export function deletePostHogPersonById(env: ServerAnalyticsEnv, analyticsId: string, fetchImpl?: typeof fetch): Promise<'queued'>
  // the bulk_delete request of 1D-T3 for an id already computed; throws AnalyticsDeletionFailed, also when POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY or POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID is unset
  // src/deletion/hooks.ts (1C declared a no-op deleteAnalyticsPerson(userId); 1D replaces it)
  export type DeletionHooks = {
    /** Inside step 'analytics-id': reads the user id from deletion_requests by request id; null without ANALYTICS_ID_KEY or for an unknown request. */
    analyticsIdOf(env: DeletionEnv, requestId: string): Promise<string | null>
    /** Inside 'delete-analytics-person' and each retry: takes only the analytics id; null deletes nothing. */
    deleteAnalyticsPerson(env: ServerAnalyticsEnv, analyticsId: string | null, deps?: { fetch?: typeof fetch; port?: (token: string) => PostHogPort }): Promise<PersonDeletion>
  }
  export const deletionHooks: DeletionHooks
  // src/deletion/workflow.ts
  export type DeletionEnv = /* 1C-T11's bindings */ & ServerAnalyticsEnv
  export const DELETION_STEPS = ['mark-account-deleting', 'mark-vault-deleting', 'purge-objects', 'erase-vault', 'delete-sign-in-records', 'analytics-id', 'delete-analytics-person', 'send-deletion-email', 'final-sweep'] as const
  export const ANALYTICS_STEP_CONFIG = { retries: { limit: 5, delay: '30 seconds', backoff: 'exponential' }, timeout: '1 minute' } as const
  export const ANALYTICS_RETRY_DAYS = 7
  ```
- Rules:
  - **`analytics-id`** is `step.do('analytics-id', STEP_CONFIG, () => deletionHooks.analyticsIdOf(this.env, requestId))`. Inside the step, the user id is read from `deletion_requests` by the request id, never from Workflow state (1C's K17), and the step answers `analyticsIdFor(userId, ANALYTICS_ID_KEY)`, or `null` without the key (then no analytics id was ever sent, 1D-T3). The analytics id is an HMAC, never the user id. It is the only value tied to the person that the Workflow keeps in its state, so the retries can still run after the final sweep has made `deletion_requests` forget the user id.
  - **`delete-analytics-person`** is `step.do('delete-analytics-person', ANALYTICS_STEP_CONFIG, () => deletionHooks.deleteAnalyticsPerson(this.env, analyticsId))` inside `try`/`catch`. Cloudflare documents that catching a step's error lets the Workflow continue (developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/sleeping-and-retrying, "Catch Workflow errors"). Five retries from 30 seconds take about 15 minutes. A caught failure logs `{ event: 'analytics_person_deletion_failed', request_id }` (the deletion request id only, never the user id or the analytics id), and steps 7 and 8 run whatever PostHog does (decided, Q15).
  - **`deleteAnalyticsPerson(env, analyticsId, deps)`:** with `null` it answers `nothing_to_delete` without a request. Otherwise it awaits `deletePostHogPersonById(env, analyticsId, deps?.fetch)` and lets `AnalyticsDeletionFailed` propagate, so the step retries. After a delete, or with nothing to delete, it sends the anonymous count: when `createServerAnalytics(env, (p) => sends.push(p), deps?.port)` is not null, `captureAnonymous('account_deleted')` and `await Promise.allSettled(sends)` (decided, Q11: a random distinct id and `$process_person_profile: false`, so the count can never recreate or join the deleted person). The step body, not the hook, then logs `analytics_person_deletion_queued` or `analytics_person_deletion_skipped` with the `request_id`; no log line carries an id of the person.
  - **After `final-sweep`,** only when `delete-analytics-person` failed: for `n` from 1 to `ANALYTICS_RETRY_DAYS`, `step.sleep(\`analytics-retry-wait-${n}\`, '1 day')` and then `step.do(\`retry-analytics-person-${n}\`, ANALYTICS_STEP_CONFIG, () => deletionHooks.deleteAnalyticsPerson(this.env, analyticsId))` inside `try`/`catch`. The loop ends at the first success. Each failure logs `analytics_person_deletion_failed` with the `request_id`; after the last one, `analytics_person_deletion_abandoned` with the `request_id`, which the owner's alert watches. The receipt (`completed`) does not wait for these retries.
  - **With 1C-T13:** 1C-T13 adds `'revoke-apple-token'` between `'erase-vault'` and `'delete-sign-in-records'`, and whichever of the two tasks lands second keeps both entries. Once both have landed, `DELETION_STEPS` is `['mark-account-deleting', 'mark-vault-deleting', 'purge-objects', 'erase-vault', 'revoke-apple-token', 'delete-sign-in-records', 'analytics-id', 'delete-analytics-person', 'send-deletion-email', 'final-sweep']`. The `retry-analytics-person-<n>` steps are named at run time after `final-sweep` and are never entries.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests.**
  - In `test/server-analytics.test.ts`: `deleting by analytics id sends the same request`: `deletePostHogPersonById(env, 'a'.repeat(64), recorder)` sends the `bulk_delete` of 1D-T3's test with `distinct_ids: ['a'.repeat(64)]`, and rejects with `AnalyticsDeletionFailed` without a request when the personal key is unset.
  - In `test/workers/deletion.test.ts`:
    - `the hook deletes the PostHog person by its analytics id and counts the deletion anonymously`: `deletionHooks.deleteAnalyticsPerson({ POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY: 'phx_test', POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID: '12345', POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN: 'phc_test' }, 'a'.repeat(64), { fetch: recorder, port: () => fakePort })`, with the recorder answering 202 `{ "deletion_errors": [] }`, resolves `'queued'`; the recorder saw one `bulk_delete` with that id; `fakePort` saw one `account_deleted` with `$process_person_profile: false` under a distinct id that is not the analytics id.
    - `the hook fails on a refusal and on a misconfiguration, and counts nothing`: a 500 rejects with `AnalyticsDeletionFailed`; a missing personal key rejects without a request; `fakePort` saw nothing either time.
    - `the analytics id is computed from the deletion request, never from the Workflow's state`: after an accepted deletion request (sleeps left on, so the run waits before the sweep), `deletionHooks.analyticsIdOf({ ...env, ANALYTICS_ID_KEY: 'k' }, requestId)` equals the HMAC of the user id under `'k'` computed in the test with `crypto.subtle`; an unknown request id gives `null`.
    - `with no analytics key, step 6 completes without a request`: a deletion run (the suite sets no analytics secret, 1D-T11) gives `waitForStepResult({ name: 'delete-analytics-person' })` equal to `'nothing_to_delete'`, and the run completes.
    - `a run whose PostHog deletion keeps failing still finishes the deletion and retries after the sweep`: `mockStepResult({ name: 'analytics-id' }, 'a'.repeat(64))`, `mockStepError` on `delete-analytics-person` and on `retry-analytics-person-1` with no `times` (every attempt), `mockStepResult({ name: 'retry-analytics-person-2' }, 'queued')`, `disableRetryDelays()` and `disableSleeps()`. The instance reaches `complete`; the request row is `completed`; `console.log` (spied) holds exactly one `jotbun-local-deletion-email` line for this request's reference and `analytics_person_deletion_failed` lines carrying the request id, and never the user id or the analytics id; `waitForStepResult({ name: 'retry-analytics-person-1' })` rejects and `retry-analytics-person-2` gives `'queued'`; and `waitForStepResult({ name: 'retry-analytics-person-3' })` raced against 500 ms gives nothing (the loop stopped at the first success).
    - `a step 6 that succeeds is not retried after the sweep`: a run without the key completes, and `waitForStepResult({ name: 'retry-analytics-person-1' })` raced against 500 ms gives nothing.
  These use the helpers 1C's suite uses (`introspectWorkflowInstance`, `modify`, `mockStepError`, `mockStepResult`, `disableRetryDelays`, `disableSleeps`, `waitForStepResult`, `waitForStatus`; all in the installed `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` 1.4.7 types).

- [ ] **Step 4: Run them and see them pass**, then 1C's deletion cases and the edge gate.
- [ ] **Step 5: Mutation check.** Return the user id instead of its HMAC from `analyticsIdOf`: the analytics-id test fails. Let `delete-analytics-person`'s failure end the Workflow (no `catch`): the keeps-failing test fails (the instance errors). Keep retrying after a success: the keeps-failing test fails at `retry-analytics-person-3`. Retry after a successful step 6: the not-retried test fails. Log the analytics id on a failure: the keeps-failing test fails.
- [ ] **Step 6: Hosted check, recorded SKIPPED:** the first real `bulk_delete` against PostHog EU waits for the project and its personal API key (Q5). PostHog's API reference lists `ids` beside `distinct_ids`; the first hosted run confirms that `distinct_ids` alone is accepted.

heading: Task 14: The account events, from 1C's credential provider
text:
**Starts after:** 1D-T1, 1C-T5

**Files:**
- Modify: `apps/app/src/auth/credentialProvider.ts` (1C-T5's)
- Test: `apps/app/src/auth/credentialProvider.test.ts` (1C-T5's)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `trackSignedIn`, `trackSignedUp`, `trackSignedOut` and `recordAnalytics` (1D-T1); `createCredentialProvider`, `SignInRequest`, `SignInResult` with `created`, `ServerSession.created`, `StoredSession` and `createFakeAuthServer` (1C-T5, from 1C's K23).
- Rules:
  - `signIn(request)` with an `active` result sends one event: `signed_up` with `request.method` when the result's `created` is true, otherwise `signed_in` with `request.method`. `created` comes from the server (1C's K23, carried as `ServerSession.created` and `SignInResult.created`), because Better Auth's own sign-in answers do not say whether they registered the account. A request's `signUp: true` never decides it: a returning Apple user may send it too. If the merged port does not expose `created` yet, every method sends `signed_in` until it does.
  - `signOut()` sends `signed_out` with `account()?.method` first, before anything else, so it is captured before `AnalyticsUpkeep` resets the identity on the session change (1D-T6). A sign-out from elsewhere (D37), a session that ends by itself and sign out everywhere send nothing in phase 1.
  - `passkey_created` is deferred: 1C records the app's passkey offer as SKIPPED, so phase 1 has nowhere that creates a passkey. The event stays in the allow-list for the phase that adds one.
  - These events are tracked before the analytics account is known; 1D-T1 holds them across the first sign-in and sends them only after yes.
  - The provider imports the emitters relatively (`../analytics/events.ts`), as Node's test runner cannot resolve the `@mobile/` alias.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests** with `recordAnalytics({ consent: 'yes' })` and 1C's fake server:
  - `the first email-code sign-in records signed_up, a later one signed_in`: 1C's fake server answers `created: true` the first time an address signs in and `false` after (K23): `signed_up` `{ method: 'email' }`, then `signed_in` `{ method: 'email' }`.
  - `a returning Apple user signing in with signUp: true records signed_in`: with a fake native Apple sign-in whose subject has signed in before, `{ method: 'apple', signUp: true }` answers `created: false` and records `signed_in` `{ method: 'apple' }`; a sign-up that answers `account_exists` records nothing.
  - `an explicit sign-out records signed_out before identity is reset`: a provider subscriber that calls `analytics.setAccount(null)` on each notification (as `AnalyticsUpkeep` does) leaves `sent` with the `signed_out` capture before the `reset`.
  - `a sign-out from elsewhere records nothing`
  - `the email address never reaches analytics`: the JSON of `sent` does not contain the test's address.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run them and see them fail.** Run: `npm run test:unit -w gogospend-app -- src/auth/credentialProvider.test.ts`. Record the counts.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** the two calls in the provider.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run them and see them pass**, then the app gate.
- [ ] **Step 5: Mutation check.** Send `signed_out` after the port's sign-out: the order test fails. Send `signed_up` whenever `signUp` is true: the returning-Apple test fails. Ignore `created`: the first-sign-in test fails.
- [ ] **Step 6: Gate, receipt, commit.** Commit: `Send the sign-in and sign-out events from the Better Auth credential provider`.

text:
**Starts after:** 1D-T5, 1D-T9, 1D-T12, 1C-T9, 1C-T12

(1C-T9 routes the approved email-code screens and the terms step after the owner's E2; 1C-T12 brings the local stack and `auth-proof.mjs`. The proof does not need 1D-T6, T7, T8, T13 or T14: PostHog stays off. The LAN change is 1D-T5's.)

**Files:**
- Modify: `docs/implementation/beta-receipts.md` (the run-sheet rows), `docs/implementation/premium-progress.md` (the closing 1D receipt), `apps/app/README.md` (development builds against `wrangler dev` on the LAN)

- [ ] **Step 1: Run the server-side proofs.** `node scripts/auth-proof.mjs` from `apps/edge` (1C-T12) and `npm run proof:live --prefix apps/edge` (1D-T12). Expected: checks 1 to 7 PASS from the first, `PASS` from the second. They stand in for the server side while the phones are SKIPPED.
- [ ] **Step 2: Write the run-sheet** into `beta-receipts.md`, each row SKIPPED until it is done on devices:
  1. On the Mac, with the migrations and settings 1C-T12's `dev.mjs` uses (copy them from it; these are their names at the time of writing): `npm run build:local --prefix apps/edge`; `npx wrangler d1 migrations apply jotbun-auth --local --persist-to .wrangler/proof -c apps/edge/wrangler.jsonc` and the same for `jotbun-erasure` (`ERASURE_DB`, R56); `npx wrangler kv key put config:v1 '<json>' --binding CONFIG --local --persist-to .wrangler/proof -c apps/edge/dist/server/wrangler.json`, the JSON being `{ "policies": … }` with 1A's `TEST_POLICIES` (`apps/edge/test/workers/support/v1-client.ts`: terms v1 required, privacy v1), since an absent `config:v1` leaves the policies unpublished and every write answers 503, and row 3's terms step needs a published version to accept; then `npx wrangler dev -c apps/edge/dist/server/wrangler.json --ip 0.0.0.0 --port 8092 --persist-to .wrangler/proof --var JOTBUN_ENV:local --var BETTER_AUTH_SECRET:<random> --var ERASURE_KEY:<random> --var COMMAND_DIGEST_KEY:<random> --var MIN_CLIENT_VERSION_IOS:1.0.0 --var MIN_CLIENT_VERSION_ANDROID:1.0.0` (each random value from `openssl rand -hex 32`, 64 characters, so `COMMAND_DIGEST_KEY` has the 32 characters it needs at least). Port 8092 matches 1C's `AUTH_BASE_URL`. If Better Auth refuses requests addressed to the LAN host, add `--var AUTH_BASE_URL:http://<the Mac's LAN IPv4>:8092` and the same for `AUTH_ISSUER`, and record it. `--ip`, `--port`, `--persist-to` and `--var` are wrangler's, as are `kv key put`'s `--binding` and `--local` (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands; checked in the installed wrangler 4.152.0). No PostHog key: analytics stays off.
  2. Two phones with a development build (Q8), `EXPO_PUBLIC_V1_API_URL=http://<the Mac's LAN IPv4>:8092`, and `EXPO_PUBLIC_REDESIGN=conflict` while that area awaits E2. Check that the build allows cleartext to the LAN address (iOS: `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` in the built `Info.plist`; Android: cleartext allowed in the debug manifest). If it does not, stop and ask the owner before changing `app.json`.
  3. Sign in on phone A, then on phone B, to the same account with email codes read from the `wrangler dev` log (two sessions). A, the account's first sign-in, shows 1C's terms step (1C's K24) for terms v1: tick the box and continue; B, signed in after that, shows no terms step.
  4. **Offline save:** History open on B. A in airplane mode; on A, Quick add ฿45 "ค่ากาแฟ": A shows it kept on the phone (`rh-offline`). Turn A's network back on at T0; note T1, when B's History shows the record. Pass: T1 − T0 is at most 20 seconds (A's socket reconnects within 15 seconds, then one flush and one poke). Three runs; record each time.
  5. **Conflict:** open the same record's edit screen on both phones. A changes the amount to ฿50 and saves. B changes it to ฿55 and saves: B shows the choice with "ของคุณ" ฿55 and "ในเซิร์ฟเวอร์" ฿50. B taps "ตัดสินใจทีหลัง": B's History shows the waiting mark; B reopens the record and the choice is still there. B chooses "ใช้ของคุณ": A's History shows ฿55 within seconds.
  6. **Sign-out:** on A, sign out everywhere from Account (a fresh sign-in by email code first). B's socket closes; B's next request shows it signed out, with any unsent record kept (D37).
  7. Screenshots of each phone at each step, in the receipt.
- [ ] **Step 3: Run what can run locally.** If development builds exist for two simulators (or a simulator and an Android emulator), run rows 3 to 6 against `wrangler dev` (the iOS Simulator reaches `http://127.0.0.1:8092`; the Android emulator reaches the host as `http://10.0.2.2:8092`, inside 10/8, which 1D-T5's rule accepts) and record the timings, marked as simulators. Real phones stay SKIPPED until the owner provides the builds (decided, Q8).
- [ ] **Step 4: The closing 1D receipt** in `premium-progress.md`: what each task proved, the mutants, the timings, every SKIPPED item with what it waits for (devices, native PostHog checks, the hosted `bulk_delete`, symbol upload), and each owner question with its default and status.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit, then the independent review of the whole 1D range** (handover §4 step 8), fixing findings test-first. Commit: `Record the phase 1 proof: the server-side proofs, the two-phone run-sheet and the 1D receipts`.

**What the proof needs from the owner (Q8):**
- Development builds of the app on two phones: the Expo/EAS project (owed), and for iPhones the Apple Developer team (ready) with both devices registered; an Android phone needs only USB debugging. The final bundle id and package name are not needed for development builds.
- The two phones on the same Wi-Fi as the Mac, and the Mac's firewall open on port 8092.
- E2 approval of 1C's email-code screens and terms step (1C-T9) and, to see the choice screen as designed, of 1D-T9's drafts (the proof can run them behind the `conflict` area before approval).
- Not needed for this proof: FCM and APNs (pokes are WebSockets, not push), the PostHog project, Apple and Google sign-in (email codes are used; 1C proves the others once the D33 accounts exist).

text:
**Starts after:** base

**Files:**

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  ```ts
  // copy/draftText.ts (pure)
  export type DraftLine = { readonly th: string; readonly en: string }
  export type DraftTable = Readonly<Record<string, DraftLine>>
  export type CopyValues = Readonly<Record<string, string | number>>
  export type WalletT = (key: string, values?: CopyValues) => string
  export function draftText(table: DraftTable, key: string, locale: 'th' | 'en' | 'vi', values?: CopyValues): string   // th: Thai; en and vi: English; {token}s filled in one pass as formatCopyValues does
  export function tableT(table: DraftTable, locale: 'th' | 'en' | 'vi'): WalletT
  // copy/useDraftCopy.ts
  export function useDraftCopy(table: DraftTable): WalletT   // locale from useActiveLocale
  // store/walletStore.ts (pure)
  export const DEVICE_PREFIX = 'jotbun.wallet.'
  export const ACCOUNT_PREFIX = 'jotbun.account.'
  export type StoreBackend = { getItem(key: string): Promise<string | null>; setItem(key: string, value: string): Promise<void>; removeItem(key: string): Promise<void>; getAllKeys(): Promise<readonly string[]>; multiRemove(keys: readonly string[]): Promise<void> }
  export type KeyValueStore = { get(name: string): Promise<string | null>; set(name: string, value: string): Promise<void>; remove(name: string): Promise<void>; eraseAll(): Promise<void> }
  export function deviceStore(backend: StoreBackend): KeyValueStore                      // 'jotbun.wallet.<name>'
  export function accountStore(backend: StoreBackend, accountId: string): KeyValueStore   // 'jotbun.account.<accountId>.<name>'; eraseAll removes only that account's keys
  // store/deviceWalletStore.ts (AsyncStorage 2.2.0 underneath)
  export function walletDeviceStore(): KeyValueStore
  export function walletAccountStore(accountId: string): KeyValueStore
  export function installStoreBackend(backend: StoreBackend | null): void   // tests only
  export function eraseDeviceSettings(): Promise<void>                       // at the sign-out erase
  export function eraseAccountKept(accountId: string): Promise<void>         // after a confirmed account deletion
  // spend/v1/spendDiary.ts
  DiaryView.accountId: string | null   // the open diary's account; null with no open diary (web, opening, locked, signed out)
  ```
- **Two scopes (R64).** Device settings (private mode and its tip, the lock, setup answers, over-budget marks, confetti marks) live in `walletDeviceStore()` and go at the sign-out erase. Wallet looks, category icons and wallet order are the person's data: `walletAccountStore(accountId)` with `useDiaryView().accountId`; they survive sign-out and go only after a confirmed deletion. With no account id nothing is stored and derived looks show.
- **The deletion erase:** in `DeleteCard`'s `settle`, read `view.accountId` before settling; when `settleDeviceCopy` answers `'erased'` and the id is not null, `await eraseAccountKept(accountId).catch(() => undefined)`. Nothing else in the deletion flow changes.
- **The copy rule for every later task:** each area keeps `src/wallet/<area>/copy.ts` exporting `export const COPY = { '<area>.<name>': { th: '…', en: '…' } } as const satisfies DraftTable`, data only (`import type { DraftTable }`). Keys are `<area>.<name>`, unique across every table, so a component that needs several areas passes the merged tables (`useDraftCopy({ ...COMMON_COPY, ...HOME_COPY })`). `common/copy.ts` (exported as `COMMON_COPY`) holds `common.close` (ปิด / Close), `common.back` (กลับ / Back), `common.next` (ถัดไป / Next, sa-lock-setup's word), `common.save` (บันทึก / Save), `common.undo` (เลิกทำ / Undo), `common.later` (ไว้ทีหลัง / Later), `common.done` (เสร็จ / Done), `common.tryAgain` (ลองอีกครั้ง / Try again), `common.amountHidden` (ซ่อนยอดเงินอยู่ / Amount hidden), `common.baht` (`{amount} บาท` / `{amount} baht`), `common.satang` (`{baht} บาท {satang} สตางค์` / `{baht} baht {satang} satang`) and `common.minus` (`ติดลบ {amount}` / `minus {amount}`, around either of the other two).

- Produces:
  ```ts
  export type AddRequest = { type?: AddType; walletId?: string; copyOf?: string };
  export type SavedContext = { lookups: Lookups; offline: boolean };
  export function AddTrayHost(props: { children: ReactNode; onSaved?: (saved: SavedEntry, context: SavedContext) => void; blocked?: boolean }): JSX.Element;
  export function useAddTray(): { open(request?: AddRequest): void; close(): void; isOpen: boolean; blocked: boolean; whenClosed(run: () => void): void };
  ```
- `whenClosed(run)` runs `run` once after the tray's Modal has hidden (its `onClosed`), or at once when no tray is open, so a second tray never opens while the first is dismissing (R69).
- `open` is the rule that starts an entry: one `Tray` (header `TypeSwitchHeader`, title from `trayTitleKey`), the draft from `firstDraft` with the request's type and wallet (`copyOf` copies as Quick add does), `openedAt = Date.now()`, and one `trackRecordStarted({ kind: type, source: 'typed' })` (1D-T7 gives the start to this rule). While `blocked` (C5) it does nothing. Outside a host it pushes `/spend/add` (today's Quick add).
- Steps: amount, then confirm (a transfer goes amount, transfer, confirm); rows open picks; picks return to confirm.
- Tell Bun: the บอกบัน row opens today's `TellBunSheet` unchanged, rendered inside the tray's content (R69). Its `onUse` fills the draft through `applyDraft` and marks the filled fields as guessed.
- Save calls `useEntrySave({ today, onSaved, savedHaptic: 'success' }).save({ draft, keypad, wallets, track: { source: guessed.size > 0 ? 'tell_bun' : 'typed', categoryKey: analyticsCategoryKey(category), openedAt } })`. The tray sends no `record_saved` (R61: 1D-T7's call in `finish` reads `track`). While `status` is `saving` the tray is `locked`. On `saved`: `onSaved(saved, { lookups, offline: saved.via === 'device' && diaryView.outcome?.status !== 'synced' })`, then close. `unconfirmed` and `conflict` show today's message with Try again or Done, as Quick add does, and the tray can be closed.

title: The saved moment: the toast, Undo and the drop into the card
heading: Task P2-T17: The saved moment: the toast, Undo and the drop into the card
text:
**Starts after:** P2-T12, P2-T16, 1D-T1

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/app/src/wallet/saved/savedMoment.ts` (pure), `saved/SavedToastHost.tsx`, `saved/SaveFlight.tsx`, `saved/copy.ts`
- Catalogue: `apps/app/src/dev/catalogue/wallet/savedSections.tsx` (`bw-saved-toast`, `bw-saved-offline`, `bw-saved-private`, `bw-saved-undone`)
- Test: `apps/app/src/wallet/saved/savedMoment.test.ts` (Node), `saved/SavedMoment.render.test.tsx`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `SavedEntry` (P2-T5); `SavedContext` (P2-T16); `useCardFrames` (P2-T12); `motionFor`, `toastEntering` (P2-T9); `walletMoneyText`, `HIDDEN_AMOUNT`, `usePrivateMode` (P2-T10); `canUndoDraft`, `openDrafts` (`src/spend/v1/redesign/shared.ts`); `trackUndoUsed` (1D-T1).
- Produces:
  ```ts
  export type SavedNotice = { recordId: string; commandId: string; kind: AddType; title: string; walletId: string | null; via: 'device' | 'online'; amountMinor: Minor; offline: boolean };
  export function noticeOf(saved: SavedEntry, lookups: Lookups, offline: boolean): SavedNotice;   // a transfer's walletId is its destination
  export type UndoPlan = { kind: 'remove_draft'; commandId: string } | { kind: 'delete_record'; recordId: string; version: 1 } | { kind: 'none' };
  export function undoPlan(notice: SavedNotice, outbox: readonly OutboxCommand[]): UndoPlan;
  export function todayOutMinor(input: { summaryExpenseMinor: Minor; confirmedIds: ReadonlySet<string>; outbox: readonly OutboxCommand[]; today: string }): Minor;   // the confirmed total plus open expense drafts dated today whose id is not confirmed
  export function toastWords(notice: SavedNotice, todayOut: Minor | null, hidden: boolean, t: WalletT): { text: string; spoken: string };
  export function SavedToastHost(props: { children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element;
  export function useSavedToast(): { show(notice: SavedNotice): void };
  export function SaveFlight(props: { notice: SavedNotice | null }): JSX.Element | null;
  ```
- `undoPlan`: a draft still on the phone that `canUndoDraft` allows is removed; a draft being sent or checked offers no Undo; a record the server holds (an online save, or a draft no longer in the outbox) is deleted at version 1, so it waits 30 days in Recently deleted.
- The toast (bw-saved, W31): `saved.toast` with today's money out; offline, `saved.toastOffline` (rh-offline) with no read. After `show`, the host reads `resources.history({ from: today, through: today, type: 'expense', sort: 'date_desc' }, undefined, HISTORY_MAX_LIMIT)` and computes `todayOutMinor` from its `summary.expense_minor` and item ids; the toast appears when the read lands or after 600 ms, whichever comes first, as `saved.toastPlain` while the total is unknown. In private mode the amount is `HIDDEN_AMOUNT` and the spoken form says `common.amountHidden`. The check is neutral (an `onToast` circle with a `toast`-coloured tick, never `under`); Undo is a `TextLink` in `toastLink` unless the plan is `none`; it enters with `toastEntering`, is announced politely, and leaves after `motion.duration.toastLong`.
- Undo is the rule (R61): `diary.removeDraft(commandId)`, or `deleteTransaction(recordId, 1, key)` under its own `useCommandKeys` key; then `saved.undone` or `saved.undoneDeleted`, and one `trackUndoUsed({ kind })`. A delete refused with `VERSION_CONFLICT` shows `saved.undoConflict` and changes nothing.
- `SaveFlight`: when `motionFor('save', reduced)` is `fly` and `frameOf(walletId)` is known, a chip with the title and the amount (`HIDDEN_AMOUNT` in private mode, R65) travels from the bottom centre to the card on the `gentle` spring, shrinking and fading; otherwise nothing travels.
- Copy: `saved.toast` บันทึกแล้ว · วันนี้ {amount}, `saved.toastPlain` บันทึกแล้ว, `saved.toastOffline` เก็บไว้ในเครื่องแล้ว · จะบันทึกเมื่อออนไลน์, `saved.undone` เลิกทำแล้ว, `saved.undoneDeleted` เลิกทำแล้ว กู้คืนได้ในรายการที่เพิ่งลบ, `saved.undoConflict` ลบไม่ได้ รายการนี้ถูกแก้ในอีกเครื่อง. Default pending owner Q3: built as written; the English lines, and any Thai line marked draft, are drafts for E2-B.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests.**
  - `savedMoment.test.ts`: `a draft never sent is removed by Undo`; `a draft being sent or checked offers no Undo`; `a record the server holds is deleted at version 1` (Review Focus 4: an online save, and a device save whose command left the outbox); `today's money out adds waiting drafts once` (a summary of `'13200'`, a waiting `'5000'` expense draft dated today and a draft whose id is confirmed give `'18200'`); `the toast follows bw-saved, and hides the amount in private mode` (`บันทึกแล้ว · วันนี้ ฿182` for `'18200'`; `บันทึกแล้ว · วันนี้ ฿••••` spoken with `ซ่อนยอดเงินอยู่`; offline, `เก็บไว้ในเครื่องแล้ว · จะบันทึกเมื่อออนไลน์`).
  - `SavedMoment.render.test.tsx`: `after a save the toast shows today's total and Undo, and its check is neutral`; `a slow total read leaves the toast saying บันทึกแล้ว after 600 ms` (`fake.hold('history')`, fake timers); `Undo removes a draft still on the phone, says เลิกทำแล้ว and sends one undo_used`; `Undo after the draft has left the phone deletes the record, which stays restorable` (Review Focus 4); `Undo refused by a newer version changes nothing and says so`; `the flying chip hides its amount in private mode` (R65); `no flight under reduced motion, or when the card is not on screen`; `Undo is a 44 pt control`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run them and see them fail.** Record the counts.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.**
- [ ] **Step 4: Run them and see them pass.**
- [ ] **Step 5: Mutation check.** Remove a draft in `sending`: the no-Undo test fails. Colour the check `under`: the neutral test fails. Show the chip's real amount: the private chip test fails.
- [ ] **Step 6: Gate, receipt, commit.** `git commit -m "Add the saved moment: today's total, Undo, a neutral check and the drop into the card"`

title: The phone's slip QR module
heading: Task P3-T1: The phone's slip QR module
text:
**Starts after:** base

**Delivers:** P3:slip-qr

A13: the native adapter is P3-T12's own file (`P3-T12 (P3:qr-native)`), whose note says who waits for it.

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/app/src/slips/slipQr.ts`, `apps/app/src/slips/qrDecoder.ts` (both pure: relative imports, no React or native import)
- Test: `apps/app/src/slips/slipQr.test.ts`, `apps/app/src/slips/qrDecoder.test.ts` (Node)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  ```ts
  // slipQr.ts
  export type SlipQr = { bankCode: string; reference: string }
  export const SLIP_QR_API_ID = '000001'
  export function crc16CcittFalse(text: string): number    // poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, over the UTF-8 bytes
  export function parseSlipQr(payload: string): SlipQr | null
  // qrDecoder.ts
  export type QrDecoder = { readonly available: boolean; decode(uri: string): Promise<readonly string[]> }
  export const noQrDecoder: QrDecoder                       // available false; decode resolves []
  export function fakeQrDecoder(byUri: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>): QrDecoder   // available true
  export function installQrDecoder(decoder: QrDecoder | null): void   // P3-T12's adapter and tests; null restores noQrDecoder
  export function getAppQrDecoder(): QrDecoder
  export function slipQrIn(decoder: QrDecoder, uri: string): Promise<SlipQr | null>   // the first payload that parses; a throwing decoder gives null
  ```
- `parseSlipQr` rules (the Thai bank slip verification QR; B14: only root `000001` counts): trim; 1 to 512 printable ASCII characters; top-level fields are a 2-digit tag, a 2-digit length and the value; exactly one root `00` whose sub-fields hold `00` = `000001`, `01` = three digits and `02` = 1 to 64 characters of `[0-9A-Za-z]` (other sub-tags ignored); `51`, when present, is `TH`; `91` comes last with length `04` and is the hex CRC of every character up to and including `9104`, compared without case. When only 1 to 3 characters follow `9104` (an app dropped leading zeros), they are left-padded with `0` and checked again. Anything else is null.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the typed stubs and the failing tests.** Stubs: `parseSlipQr` returns null, `crc16CcittFalse` returns 0, `slipQrIn` resolves null.
  ```ts
  test('a Thai bank slip QR gives its sending bank and reference', () => {
    assert.deepEqual(parseSlipQr('004000060000010103002021900021231231212000115102TH91049C30'), { bankCode: '002', reference: '0002123123121200011' })
    assert.deepEqual(parseSlipQr(' 00390006000001010300402180162981055123456785102TH91043BF7 '), { bankCode: '004', reference: '016298105512345678' })
  })
  test('the CRC covers everything up to 9104 and is read in either case', () => {
    assert.equal(crc16CcittFalse('004000060000010103002021900021231231212000115102TH9104'), 0x9c30)
    assert.ok(parseSlipQr('004000060000010103002021900021231231212000115102TH91049c30'))
    assert.equal(parseSlipQr('004000060000010103002021900021231231212000115102TH91049C31'), null)
  })
  test('a CRC whose leading zero was dropped is padded back', () => {
    assert.deepEqual(parseSlipQr('00390006000001010301402180163000000000000035102TH910445A'), { bankCode: '014', reference: '016300000000000003' })
  })
  test('TrueMoney and payment QR codes are not bank slips', () => {
    assert.equal(parseSlipQr('00480002010102010203P2P0313TXN00012345670408250120249104b425'), null)
    assert.equal(parseSlipQr('0002010102115802TH6304ABCD'), null)
  })
  test('a slip-shaped QR whose root is not 000001 is not a bank slip (B14)', () => {
    assert.equal(parseSlipQr('004000060000020103002021900021231231212000115102TH91044531'), null)   // root 000002, CRC 4531 valid
  })
  ```
  Also `anything malformed is null`: a length longer than the text, a root without `02`, `51` = `US`, a reference with a space, 513 characters, and a payload whose `91` is not last. `qrDecoder.test.ts`: `noQrDecoder is unavailable and finds nothing`; `slipQrIn returns the first payload that is a bank slip` (a fake decoder answering `['https://example.test', <the 004 slip>]` gives bank `004`); `a decoder that throws finds no slip`; `installQrDecoder replaces the app's decoder and null restores noQrDecoder`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run them and see them fail.** Run: `npm run test:unit -w gogospend-app -- src/slips/slipQr.test.ts src/slips/qrDecoder.test.ts`.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** the parser, the CRC and the decoder registry as the rules say.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run them and see them pass.**
- [ ] **Step 5: Mutation check.** Skip the CRC comparison: the wrong-CRC case fails. Accept any root id: the `000002` case fails. Drop the padding: the dropped-zero case fails.
- [ ] **Step 6: Gate, receipt, commit.** `git commit -m "Read Thai bank slip QR codes on the phone, with their CRC, behind a decoder port"`

title: The gateway transport, one deadline per request and the call trace
heading: Task P3-T4: The gateway transport, one deadline per request and the call trace
text:
**Starts after:** 1B-T13

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/edge/src/v1/ai/transport.ts`
- Modify: `apps/edge/src/v1/env.ts` (`AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN?: string`), `src/v1/handler.ts` (`V1Deps.transport` replaces 1B-T7's `send`; each request's context gets `deps.transport !== undefined ? deps.transport : transportFromEnv(env)`), `src/v1/worker-routes.ts` (`WorkerContext.transport` replaces 1B-T7's `send`), `src/v1/ai/service.ts` (deps take `transport` for `send`; every call goes through `tracedSend` with the request's trace and, until P3-T6, `new AiDeadline(25_000)`, today's timeout), `src/v1/ai/routes.ts` (the service gets `w.transport`), `src/server/ai/model.ts` (delete `anthropicSender` and `SendMessage`), `test/support/fake-model.ts` (a `transport`; replies may name their model; `apiFailure(status, headers?)` and `hang()`, which rejects with `APIConnectionTimeoutError` once the call's `timeoutMs` has passed), `test/workers/support/v1-client.ts` (`startV1` option `transport` replaces `send`), `apps/edge/README.md` and `wrangler.jsonc` comments (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is the gateway URL; secrets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN`)
- Test: `apps/edge/test/ai-transport.test.ts` (Node); 1B-T7's `test/workers/ai.test.ts` runs on the new option

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `MessageParams`, `ModelMessage` (`src/server/ai/model.ts`); `VaultAiService`, `AI_FEATURES` (1B-T7, contracts); `flag` (`src/server/env.ts`).
- Produces:
  ```ts
  export const AI_GATEWAY_HEADERS = { 'cf-aig-collect-log': 'false', 'cf-aig-skip-cache': 'true' } as const
  export const MIN_CALL_MS = 2_000
  export type ModelTransport = { send(params: MessageParams, options: { timeoutMs: number }): Promise<ModelMessage> }
  export function anthropicTransport(config: { apiKey: string; baseURL?: string; gatewayToken?: string; fetch?: typeof fetch }): ModelTransport
  export function transportFromEnv(env: Pick<V1Env, 'AI_ENABLED' | 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' | 'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL' | 'AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN'>): ModelTransport | null
  export type CallFailure = 'rate_limited' | 'server_error' | 'timeout' | 'no_connection' | 'rejected' | 'other'
  export function callFailure(error: unknown): CallFailure
  export class AiDeadline { constructor(totalMs: number, now?: () => number); remainingMs(): number; child(capMs: number): AiDeadline }   // child: ends at the earlier of this deadline and capMs from now, on the same clock
  export class DeadlinePassed extends Error {}
  export type RecordedCall = { spanId: string; feature: AiFeature; requested: string; model: string; escalated: boolean; latencyMs: number; sent: boolean;
    httpStatus: number | null; retryAfterSeconds: number | null; failure: CallFailure | null; stopReason: string | null; usage: { input: number; output: number; cacheRead: number; cacheWrite: number } | null }
  export type AiTrace = { readonly id: string; readonly calls: RecordedCall[]; analytics: 'yes' | 'no' | 'unasked' }
  export function newTrace(): AiTrace   // a fresh UUID; analytics 'unasked' until P3-T10 reads the consent
  export function tracedSend(transport: ModelTransport, trace: AiTrace, deadline: AiDeadline, call: { feature: AiFeature; escalated: boolean; params: MessageParams; capMs?: number }): Promise<ModelMessage>
  // handler.ts: V1Deps.transport?: ModelTransport | null; worker-routes.ts: WorkerContext.transport: ModelTransport | null (P4-T6's slips route reads it too)
  ```
- `anthropicTransport`: `new Anthropic({ apiKey, baseURL: baseURL || undefined, maxRetries: 0, defaultHeaders, fetch })`: no retry inside a call, so a 429's `APIError` reaches `tracedSend` with its headers (B27, A26; SDK 1.2.0 would sleep out `retry-after` and end as `APIUserAbortError`). `defaultHeaders` = `AI_GATEWAY_HEADERS` plus `cf-aig-authorization: Bearer <gatewayToken>` when given (default pending owner Q4: none); `send` calls `client.beta.messages.create(params, { timeout: timeoutMs, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) })`. `transportFromEnv` is null unless `flag(AI_ENABLED)` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- `tracedSend`: the call's time is `min(deadline.remainingMs(), capMs)`; below `MIN_CALL_MS` it records a `timeout` call with `sent: false` and throws `DeadlinePassed` without sending. Otherwise it records `sent: true`, `model` (`message.model`, else `params.model`), `httpStatus` (200, or the `APIError`'s status), `retryAfterSeconds` (a failed `APIError`'s `retry-after` in whole seconds, 1 to 3,600, else null), `stopReason`, `usage` (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0`, `cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0`) and the latency, then returns or rethrows.
- `callFailure`: `DeadlinePassed`, `APIUserAbortError` and `APIConnectionTimeoutError` are `timeout`; any other `APIConnectionError` is `no_connection`; an `APIError` with status 429 is `rate_limited`, 500 and above `server_error`, any other status `rejected`; anything else `other`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Stub, then write the failing tests** in `ai-transport.test.ts`, with a recording `fetch` that answers a JSON message. Stubs: the transport sends no headers, `callFailure` returns `other`, `tracedSend` records nothing.
  - `every request goes to the gateway with logging and caching off`: `baseURL` `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/acct/gw/anthropic`: the URL starts with that plus `/v1/messages`; headers `cf-aig-collect-log: false`, `cf-aig-skip-cache: true`, `x-api-key: sk-test`; no `cf-aig-authorization`.
  - `the gateway token is sent only when set`: `gatewayToken: 't0k'` sends `cf-aig-authorization: Bearer t0k`.
  - `a call that outlives its time fails as a timeout and is recorded`: a `fetch` that settles only by rejecting with an `AbortError` when its `init.signal` aborts (the SDK awaits it), `new AiDeadline(2_100)`: rejects within 3 s; `callFailure` is `timeout`; the trace holds one call with `failure: 'timeout'` and `httpStatus: null`.
  - `a rate limit fails at once as rate_limited with its wait`: a `fetch` answering 429 with `retry-after: 40`, `new AiDeadline(25_000)`: rejects within 2 s after one `fetch`; `callFailure` is `rate_limited`; the recorded call has `httpStatus: 429` and `retryAfterSeconds: 40`.
  - `a request with less than 2 s left makes no call`: `new AiDeadline(1_000)`: `DeadlinePassed`, `fetch` never called, one recorded `timeout` with `sent: false`.
  - `a child deadline ends at the earlier of its cap and its parent` (a fake clock: a 55 s parent's 25 s child reads 25,000; 40 s into a 45 s parent, a 25 s child reads 5,000).
  - `callFailure names each failure` (the mapping above, with `APIError.generate` for 429, 529, 500 and 400, and one instance of each connection and abort error).
  - `the trace keeps the reply's model, status, stop reason and tokens`: a reply naming `claude-haiku-5-5` with usage `{ input_tokens: 120, output_tokens: 40, cache_read_input_tokens: 10, cache_creation_input_tokens: null }` records `{ model: 'claude-haiku-5-5', httpStatus: 200, stopReason: 'end_turn', usage: { input: 120, output: 40, cacheRead: 10, cacheWrite: 0 } }`.
  - `transportFromEnv is null unless AI is on and keyed`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run them and see them fail.** Run: `npm run test:edge -- test/ai-transport.test.ts`.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** the module, swap the service's sender for the transport (behaviour otherwise unchanged; models stay as 1B-T7 left them until P3-T6) and move the fake and `startV1` to `transport`.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run them and see them pass,** then `npm run test:edge:workers -- test/workers/ai.test.ts` (1B-T7's 17 ported cases plus its two, unchanged).
- [ ] **Step 5: Mutation check.** Drop `cf-aig-collect-log`: the gateway test fails. Ignore the deadline in `tracedSend`: the less-than-2-s test fails. Read 529 as `rejected`: the failure case fails. Set `maxRetries: 1`: the rate-limit case fails.
- [ ] **Step 6: Gate, receipt, commit.** Recorded for P6C (A20): every environment with `AI_ENABLED` true sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to its gateway, or calls skip AI Gateway (§6.7). `git commit -m "Send every model call through AI Gateway with logging and caching off, under one deadline, recorded in a trace"`

text:

- Produces:
  ```ts
  // contracts
  export const SLIP_KINDS = ['slip', 'receipt', 'unreadable'] as const
  export type SlipKind = (typeof SLIP_KINDS)[number]
  // AiSlipResult gains kind: SlipKind; declined: boolean; tokens: { input: number; output: number }
  // src/v1/ai/slip-read.ts
  export type SlipImage = { base64: string; mediaType: AiSlipMediaType }
  export type SlipRead = { kind: SlipKind; drafts: AiDraft[]; bank: string | null; model: ModelTier; escalated: boolean; declined: boolean; tokens: { input: number; output: number } }
  export class SlipNotRead extends Error { constructor(readonly failure: CallFailure) }
  export type HaikuOutcome = { kind: 'answer'; read: { kind: SlipKind; drafts: AiDraft[] } } | { kind: 'declined' } | { kind: 'unusable' } | { kind: 'failed'; failure: CallFailure }
  export function slipNeedsOpus(outcome: HaikuOutcome): boolean
  export function readSlipImage(input: { image: SlipImage; context: DraftContext; locale: AiLocale }, deps: { transport: ModelTransport; trace: AiTrace; deadline: AiDeadline }): Promise<SlipRead>
  ```
- `SLIP_SYSTEM` gains: `- kind: "slip" for a bank or e-wallet transfer slip, "receipt" for a shop receipt or bill, "unreadable" when no amount can be read; with "unreadable" return 0 drafts.` A read with no draft is `unreadable`; an `unreadable` answer's drafts are dropped. A reply whose `kind` is missing or not one of the three is `unusable`. `declined` is true when any call of the read stopped with `refusal`; `tokens` adds every call's input (with cache reads and writes) and output.
- `slipNeedsOpus` (D25's triggers, H6): true for `declined`, `unusable` (truncated, not JSON or no `kind`), no draft, a null `amount_minor`, a `date_guessed` flag, or a `slip` expense draft with a null `merchant`; false for `failed`.

Otherwise Opus (`opusRequest('medium', 8_000)`, the same image and text, `escalated: true`): Opus drafts win; else Haiku's, if any; else `unreadable` when Opus answered, or `SlipNotRead`. It neither consumes nor refunds a use; its callers do.
- The slip route answers `{ drafts, bank, source: 'ai', model, escalated, kind, declined, tokens }`; on `SlipNotRead` it refunds when `shouldRefund(trace.calls, false)` (a 400 `rejected` spends the use, A14) and answers 503 `AI_PAUSED` with `retryAfterSeconds` 300.

  - `Opus re-reads when the amount does not parse, the date is implausible, or a slip has no receiver` (`it.each`: `amount_baht: null`; a date next year; `merchant: null`): two calls, the second with `model: 'claude-opus-5-5'`, `betas: ['server-side-fallback-2026-07-01']`, `fallbacks: 'default'` and the same image `data`; the result says Opus and `escalated: true`.
  - `a Haiku refusal is re-read by Opus and marked declined`; `an answer that is not JSON, or has no draft, is re-read by Opus`; `a guessed category or wallet never escalates`; `a receipt, or an income slip, without a receiver is not re-read`.
  - `when Opus also finds nothing the slip is unreadable` (`kind: 'unreadable'`, `drafts: []`, Opus, escalated).
  - `Opus failing after a Haiku draft keeps Haiku's draft` (Review Focus 3: Haiku's amount is null, Opus answers 529; the result is Haiku's draft with `escalated: true`; `remaining.slip` 9).
  - `a Haiku refusal followed by an Opus outage is 503 AI_PAUSED and gives the use back` (Review Focus 3: Haiku `refusal()`, Opus 529; two recorded calls; `remaining.slip` 10).
  - `an outage on Haiku is 503 AI_PAUSED, with no Opus call and the use given back` (Haiku 529).
  - `an escalated read spends one use` (`remaining.slip` 9).
  - `both requests carry the same bytes through the gateway, and nothing is kept`: with `anthropicTransport` over a recording `fetch` that scripts both replies, both requests carry `cf-aig-collect-log: false`; R2 holds nothing under any of the vault's prefixes; `import_uploads` is empty; `ai_usage` is exactly `[{ feature: 'slip', uses: 1 }]`; a console spy saw no part of the base64.

title: Ask Bun asks Opus again in a fresh conversation
heading: Task P3-T9: Ask Bun asks Opus again in a fresh conversation
text:

**Interfaces:**

- Produces:
  ```ts
  // contracts
  export type AiFigureScope = { from: string; through: string; type: AiDraftType; category_id: string | null }
  export type AiFigure = { label: string; amount_minor: Minor; count: number | null; scope: AiFigureScope | null }
  // src/v1/ai/ask.ts
  export const ASK_MAX_TURNS = 5
  export type AskOutcome = { kind: 'grounded'; answer: string; figures: AiFigure[] }
    | { kind: 'ungrounded' | 'declined' | 'no_answer'; figures: AiFigure[] } | { kind: 'failed'; failure: CallFailure; figures: AiFigure[] }
  export type AskDeps = { transport: ModelTransport; trace: AiTrace; deadline: AiDeadline; tool(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<{ result: unknown; figures: AiFigure[]; allow: Allowance } | { error: string }> }
  export function runAskConversation(tier: ModelTier, input: { question: string; today: string; locale: AiLocale; categories: readonly { id: string; name: string }[] }, deps: AskDeps): Promise<AskOutcome>
  export function askWithEscalation(input: Parameters<typeof runAskConversation>[1], deps: AskDeps): Promise<{ answer: string; figures: AiFigure[]; source: 'ai' | 'facts'; model: AiModel; escalated: boolean } | { paused: true }>
  ```
- `runAskConversation` keeps today's loop (at most `ASK_MAX_TURNS` turns, its own `AllowedNumbers` and figures): a grounded text is `grounded`; an ungrounded one `ungrounded`; `refusal` `declined`; the turn limit, a truncated or empty answer, or a turn that cannot start in time (`DeadlinePassed`) `no_answer`; a call failure `failed`.
- `askWithEscalation`: Haiku under `deps.deadline.child(HAIKU_ASK_CAP_MS)`, so H3's cap covers its whole conversation; `grounded` answers (`model: HAIKU`); `ungrounded`, `declined` or `no_answer` start Opus from scratch under the parent deadline: one user message equal to Haiku's first, the same `system` and `tools`, `opusRequest('medium', 12_000)`, `escalated: true` on its calls. Opus `grounded` answers (`model: OPUS, escalated: true`); otherwise `figuresText(figures, locale)` over Opus's figures, else Haiku's (Bun's could-not-find line when neither has any), with `source: 'facts', model: 'rules'`, as today. Only when the conversation that ended the request is `failed` and no figures exist is it `{ paused: true }` (503 `AI_PAUSED`). A Haiku `failed` never reaches Opus.
- `aiTool` figures: `spending_total` carries `count` (its n) and `scope` `{ from, through, type, category_id }`; `category_totals` each row's n and a scope naming that category; `top_merchants` its n and `scope: null`; `budget_status` `count: null, scope: null`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Stub, then write the failing tests.** Stub: `askWithEscalation` runs Haiku only.
  - `an answer that fails the grounding check is asked again of Opus in a fresh conversation`: Haiku calls `spending_total`, then writes `฿999`; Opus's first request has exactly one message, role `user`, equal to Haiku's first message, and the same `system` and `tools`; Opus's grounded answer comes back as `{ source: 'ai', model: 'claude-opus-5-5', escalated: true }`.
  - `a Haiku refusal goes to Opus`; `five Haiku tool turns without an answer go to Opus`.
  - `when Opus is not grounded either, the plain figures answer` (`source: 'facts', model: 'rules', escalated: true`, Opus's figures).
  - `a Haiku outage never reaches Opus` (a 429 after one tool turn: Haiku's figures as facts, `escalated: false`, the use given back).
  - `an ungrounded Haiku answer followed by an Opus outage answers Haiku's figures and gives the use back` (Review Focus 3: `source: 'facts'`, `model: 'rules'`, `escalated: true`, `remaining.ask` 20).
  - `a question neither model grounds, with no figures, answers that Bun could not find it` (200, `source: 'facts'`, บันหาข้อมูลนี้ในบันทึกของคุณไม่เจอ, `remaining.ask` 19).
  - `an escalated question counts once` (`remaining.ask` 19); `the prompts carry no account, session or device identifier (both conversations)`.
  - `ask-deadline.test.ts`: `a slow Haiku conversation is cut at 25 s and Opus still answers` (a fake clock and transport: each Haiku tool turn takes 12 s, so the third cannot start under the child deadline and Haiku ends `no_answer`; Opus's first call is given 31,000 ms, and its grounded answer comes back with `escalated: true`).
  - `figures carry their record count and scope` (a `spending_total` for 1 to 24 October over food gives `count: 41` in a seeded vault with 41 such records and `scope: { from: '2026-10-01', through: '2026-10-24', type: 'expense', category_id: <food> }`; a merchant figure has a count and `scope: null`; budget figures have both null).
  - App: `figures need count and scope`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run them and see them fail.** Run: `npm run test:edge -- test/ask-deadline.test.ts`, `npm run test:edge:workers -- test/workers/ask-escalation.test.ts` and `npm run test:unit -w gogospend-app -- src/spend/v1/ai/aiResources.test.ts`.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.**
- [ ] **Step 4: Run them and see them pass,** with `ai.test.ts`, `ai-routing.test.ts` and `ai-uses.test.ts`.
- [ ] **Step 5: Mutation check.** Replay Haiku's turns to Opus: the fresh-conversation case fails. Escalate on a 429: the outage case fails. Consume a second use for Opus: the counts-once case fails. Give Haiku the parent deadline: the slow-conversation case fails. Answer paused whenever no figures exist: the could-not-find case fails.
- [ ] **Step 6: Gate, receipt, commit.** Client minimum `AI_MIN_CLIENT_VERSION`. `git commit -m "Ask Opus again in a fresh conversation when Haiku's answer is ungrounded, declined or unfinished, and give each figure its count and scope"`

- Create: `apps/app/src/wallet/photos/drafts.ts`, `photoModel.ts` (pure), `photoPort.ts`, `AttachStep.tsx`, `PhotoRow.tsx`, `CameraOff.tsx`; `apps/app/locales/th.json`, `apps/app/locales/en.json`; sections `bw-attach`, `bw-attach-offline`, `bw-attach-slip-qr`, `bw-camera-off`, `bw-tray-confirm-photo`
- Modify: `apps/app/src/wallet/add/addFlow.ts` (`AddStep` gains `'attach'` and `'consent'`), `AmountStep.tsx` (`onAttach?: () => void`; the แนบรูป row only with `onAttach` and while `usePhotosArea()`), `ConfirmStep.tsx` (`photo?: PhotoRowProps | null`), `AddTrayHost.tsx` (`onAttach`, the photo, the attach and consent steps, `hasPhoto`), `apps/app/app.json` (`["expo-image-picker", { "photosPermission": "Jotbun opens your photos only when you choose a receipt or slip.", "cameraPermission": "Jotbun uses the camera only when you take a photo of a receipt or slip.", "microphonePermission": false }]`, `ios.infoPlist.CFBundleAllowMixedLocalizations: true`, `locales: { th: './locales/th.json', en: './locales/en.json' }`)
- Test: `apps/app/src/wallet/photos/photoModel.test.ts`, `photoPort.test.ts` (Node), `AttachStep.render.test.tsx`

**Interfaces:**

- Produces:
  ```ts
  // photoModel.ts
  export type PickedPhoto = { bytes: Uint8Array; contentType: AttachmentContentType; dataUri: string; slipQr: SlipQr | null }   // A27's name; a structural superset of receiptModel.ts's PickedPhoto, so receiptFile takes it
  export function photoOffline(view: Pick<DiaryView, 'phase' | 'outcome'> | null): boolean        // an open diary whose last run is 'waiting' or 'paused'
  export function readableByBun(photo: PickedPhoto): { ok: true; base64: string; mediaType: AiSlipMediaType } | { ok: false; reason: 'too_large' }   // AI_SLIP_MAX_BYTES; no resizer (default pending owner Q2)
  export function photoProblem(bytes: number, contentType: string): 'too_large' | 'unsupported' | 'empty' | null   // receiptFile's rules: 12 MiB, JPEG, PNG, WebP
  // photoPort.ts
  export type PhotoSource = 'camera' | 'album'
  export type PhotoPick = { kind: 'picked'; photo: PickedPhoto } | { kind: 'cancelled' } | { kind: 'denied'; source: PhotoSource; canAskAgain: boolean }
    | { kind: 'unavailable' } | { kind: 'refused'; reason: 'too_large' | 'unsupported' | 'empty' }
  export type PhotoPicker = { pick(source: PhotoSource): Promise<PhotoPick> }
  export function expoPhotoPicker(deps?: { decoder?: QrDecoder; imagePicker?: () => Promise<typeof import('expo-image-picker')>; file?: (uri: string) => { bytes(): Promise<Uint8Array>; delete(): void } }): PhotoPicker
  export function fakePhotoPicker(answers: readonly PhotoPick[]): PhotoPicker & { calls: PhotoSource[] }
  // PhotoRow.tsx, AttachStep.tsx
  export type PhotoRowProps = { state: 'kept' | 'not_read' | 'slip_not_kept' | 'offline'; onRemove(): void }
  export function PhotoRow(props: PhotoRowProps): JSX.Element
  export function AttachStep(props: { offline: boolean; aiEnabled: boolean; readWithBun: boolean; onReadWithBun(on: boolean): void; onPicked(photo: PickedPhoto): void; picker?: PhotoPicker }): JSX.Element
  ```
- `expoPhotoPicker`: the camera asks `requestCameraPermissionsAsync()` first; then `launchCameraAsync` or `launchImageLibraryAsync` with `{ mediaTypes: ['images'], allowsEditing: false, exif: false, quality: 0.6 }` (the album also `allowsMultipleSelection: false` and `preferredAssetRepresentationMode: Compatible`); then, on the picker's own file, `slipQrIn`, `new File(uri).bytes()`, `photoProblem`, and `new File(uri).delete()` (best effort). The photo then lives only in memory as bytes and a data URI (H10). The base `ReceiptPicker` is not reused.
- The host holds one photo; its row (B3): a `slipQr` photo is `slip_not_kept` (Bun may still read it); with the read off any other is `kept`; with the read on it is `not_read` until P3-T17's read answers `receipt`, and stays so after a failure, the day's limit or a photo too large for Bun, until the read is turned off (then it is a photo attached without asking Bun). While `photoOffline` the rows are `offline`. The read toggle shows only while `useBunAiArea()`; without it the read is off. The read starts on when AI is on (as bw-attach draws it) and off when AI is off, not remembered; turning it on with AI off opens the `'consent'` step, and agreeing returns with it on. A denied camera sends one `trackPermissionDenied({ permission: 'camera' })`; a denied album sends one with `permission: 'photos'` and shows `photosOff`. The save passes `hasPhoto` only for a `kept` photo.
- Copy (`photos.*`, read as P3-T14 says). From bw-attach, in order: `attachTitle`, `camera`, `cameraLine`, `album`, `albumLine`, `readToggle`, `readToggleLine`, `footnote` (the retention consent, H10). From bw-tray-confirm: `row` (รูป), `receiptCount`, `remove` (the remove button's label, ลบรูป). From es-camera-denied, in order: `cameraOffTitle` (its two parts as one line), `cameraOffBody`, `cameraOffWhere`, `cameraOffStep1`, `cameraOffStep2`, `cameraOffKept`, `openSettings`. Drafts: `offline` ต้องต่อเน็ตเพื่อแนบรูป รายการยังบันทึกได้ตามปกติ; `slipNotKept` รูปนี้เป็นสลิป Jotbun ไม่เก็บรูปสลิป ให้บันอ่านยอดแทนได้; `unread` บันยังไม่ได้อ่านรูปนี้เป็นใบเสร็จ จึงยังไม่เก็บ ปิดการให้บันอ่านเพื่อเก็บไว้; `tooLarge` รูปนี้ใหญ่เกิน 12 MB เลือกรูปอื่น; `unsupported` ใช้รูป JPEG, PNG หรือ WebP; `cameraOffWhereAndroid` เปิดได้ในการตั้งค่าของเครื่อง; `photosOff` Jotbun ยังเปิดอัลบั้มไม่ได้ เปิดสิทธิ์รูปภาพได้ในการตั้งค่า. The locale files hold `ios.NSCameraUsageDescription` and `ios.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription`, Thai drafts Jotbun ใช้กล้องเมื่อคุณกดถ่ายรูปใบเสร็จหรือสลิปเท่านั้น and Jotbun เปิดอัลบั้มเมื่อคุณเลือกรูปใบเสร็จหรือสลิปเท่านั้น, English as the plugin's. Deviations: no recent-photos strip (no media library package), so รูปล่าสุด, ดูทั้งหมด and its photo labels are skipped; no capture time.

  - `photoPort.test.ts` (injected picker, file and decoder modules): `the camera asks permission first and says when it was refused`; `a picked photo is read into memory and the picker's copy is deleted` (`delete` once, on the asset's URI); `a photo whose QR is a bank slip says so`; `a photo over 12 MiB is refused`.
